cultural.vision_reason: This is a traditional Ethiopian church-style painting on cotton depicting Emperor Tewodros II's court of judgement, with figures in Amhara royal and clerical dress (shammas, embroidered lemd capes, turbans) — a genuine example of Amhara/Ethiopian courtly religious painting.

physical.title: painting
physical.summary: Painting on cotton depicting the court of judgement of Emperor Tewodros II. He is shown seated between two lions beneath the silk brocade canopy of a royal tent. He is wearing traditional Ethiopian dress of a long silk tunic and white shamma and is carrying a spear. All around the royal tent are the Emperor's retainers with raised swords. To the left are seated the clergy  wearing embroidered capes (lemd) and white turbans with open books in their hands. In front of the Emperor in the foreground of the painting are five Rases (dukes) each a wearing richly embroidered velvet lemd (cape). On the left hand side are images of the punishments inflicted on those who have been judged by Tewodros' court to have transgressed the law.
